strengths: Well-motivated asymmetry problem in modality alignment with clear intuition
Solid theoretical contributions with rigorous proofs (Theorems 1 and Propositions 1-2)
Comprehensive experimental evaluation across multiple datasets, settings (few-shot, base-to-novel, etc.), and metrics
Consistent improvements across all evaluation protocols, with notable gains in hierarchical metrics (28.83% HCA improvement)
Strong visualization and interpretability analysis (T-SNE, GradCAM attention maps) demonstrating learned hierarchical features
Detailed ablation studies validating each component's contribution
Good reproducibility effort with extensive appendices and promise of code release
weaknesses: Taylor approximation in Theorem 1 lacks rigor—no error bounds provided for the approximation quality
Core assumption about heterogeneous manifolds is not empirically validated—actual learned curvature values not analyzed or visualized
Marginal gains from heterogeneous manifolds (HypV1 to full method often <1%), undermining the central motivation
Key design choices poorly justified: disabling cross-token self-attention, selecting layers 4&7 for intermediate features, fixed δ parameter—lack empirical validation
No statistical significance testing despite modest improvements in many settings (1-3%); results averaged over only 3 runs without error bars
Limited baseline comparisons—hyperbolic methods only in one table; main comparisons are with MaPLe/PromptSRC variants
Computational cost and complexity not analyzed; practical implementation details missing (golden section search tolerance, gradient computation numerics)
Evaluation scope narrow—limited to TOS classification tasks; generalization to other hierarchical vision-language problems unclear
Novelty is incremental—primarily combines existing techniques (cross-attention, hyperbolic embeddings, entailment cones) rather than introducing fundamentally new concepts
